A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Nova and contain readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original decompilation and binary-similarity experiments, ablations, embedding analyses, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v5 reports original results for both tasks, including expanded decompilation comparisons and a new attention-head ablation.

M1.justification: The three attention patterns, half-head application, contrastive objectives, and downstream procedures remain unchanged. Mixed text/assembly attention was already documented in v3 Appendix A.2. Granite and all-head variants are experimental comparisons, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use AnghaBench, The-Stack, BinaryCorp-3M, HumanEval-Decompile, and the same six binary-similarity benchmarks. The added comparisons evaluate different models or attention configurations within existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Table 2 adds CodeLlama, StarCoder2, DeepSeekCoder, Qwen-2.5-Coder, and LLMCompiler, and replaces GPT-4 with GPT-4o in the aggregate decompilation comparison. Tables 3–4 additionally evaluate Granite variants and LongCoder attention. The binary-similarity comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Granite-3B fine-tuning controls, a shared DeepSeekCoder-1.3B backbone for comparing attention designs, and an all-head masking configuration. Decompilation ablations also report Pass@10. Existing training budgets, truncation limits, decoding settings, datasets, and binary-similarity pool sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds tests of complementarity with long-context training, alternative attention designs, and half versus all hierarchical heads. It removes v3 Figure 6's attention-entropy and instruction-token profiles and Figure 13's quantitative embedding-distance analyses. PCA, t-SNE, case studies, and detailed binary-similarity ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Removing v3 Figure 13 eliminates box-and-whisker summaries of embedding-distance distributions. These describe dispersion across code examples, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the 20 sampled decompilations per assembly remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Decompilation scores are extensively revised: Nova-6B's reported average Pass@1/Pass@10 changes from 29.42/39.83 to 34.36/46.91, alongside revised baseline and ablation scores. v5 adds results for the expanded comparisons and controls. Binary-similarity scores remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the score revisions sufficiently to attribute them to a procedural improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss functions retain their substance. v5 omits the separately displayed optimization-order inequality, but preserves its explanation and the same hinge-loss formulation. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central method and outperformance claims remain. The abstract and introduction replace the 146.54% relative decompilation improvement with 14.84–21.58 percentage-point improvements, and model availability replaces the analysis contribution bullet. The conclusion nevertheless retains the old 146.54% figure.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations concerning complementarity with long-context training, instruction-aware versus fixed-window attention, and knowledge lost through all-head masking. Interpretations based on the removed entropy and embedding-distance analyses disappear. The X86-only and model-scale limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds two Nova model-release links and explicitly identifies averaged last-layer instruction-token hidden states as function embeddings. Existing preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, and software disclosures are retained. These additions document access and implementation rather than establish changed training procedures.

R1.justification: New Section 5.3 substantially expands positioning against hierarchical and long-context attention, discussing LongCoder, CAST, PA-former, HierarchyNet, and attention sinks. Additional coverage of LLMCompiler, Granite, StarCoder2, and Qwen connects the expanded experiments to newer competing approaches.

P1.justification: Most explanatory prose and the overall narrative are retained. Local revisions move mixed-input attention into Section 2.2, reorganize results and appendix discussions, reverse the conclusion/limitations order, and update authorship and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Decompilation tables merge Pass@1 and Pass@10, Figure 3 incorporates the former appendix attention diagram, and embedding plots move between the main text and appendix. New comparison tables, removed diagnostic plots, and reformatted attention heatmaps substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader relevant baselines, the shared-backbone LongCoder comparison, and the all-head ablation strengthen validation of Nova's design. Model-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by removal of quantitative embedding and attention diagnostics, unexplained decompilation-score revisions, and the conclusion's unreconciled 146.54% claim.
